mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with broader economic slowdowns and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and economic slowdowns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS declines do not correlate with subsequent corporate revenue declines.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases do not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not significantly predict negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with subsequent consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same period, the combination signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY decline > 10% and UNRATE increase > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between HOUST and UNRATE does not significantly predict negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of economic expansion, a sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 increases do not correlate with subsequent earnings growth during expansions.
